Roofing in Benbrook, Texas

Benbrook keeps a register of contractors, each with at least $300,000 in liability insurance on file. One free number, answered around the clock, connects you with an independent roofing company in southwest Tarrant County.

Call (469) 649-7066 Benbrook registration

  2. Service Areas
  3. Benbrook

A lake city with a contractor register

Benbrook sits southwest of Fort Worth in Tarrant County, a city of 24,520 people at the 2020 census, wrapped around the north end of Benbrook Lake. The lake is a flood control reservoir on the Clear Fork of the Trinity River. The Army Corps of Engineers began the dam in May 1947, finished it in December 1950, and started holding water in September 1952.

For roofing in Benbrook, the city's contractor rules are the most useful fact. Benbrook's FAQ says work in the city must be performed by a contractor registered with Benbrook (it lists one exception, for owners with a homestead exemption on file). Registration asks for the owner's driver's license, any state trade license, and proof of at least $300,000 in liability insurance, and it lapses one year after the application.

DFW Expert Roofers is a free phone line, not a Benbrook roofer. Dial it and an automated voice asks what happened up top, then routes you to an independent, locally owned roofing company in the area. The roofing company does the inspecting, pricing and work, and bills you directly.

Checking a roofer against Benbrook's records

Based on the City of Benbrook's permit FAQ, its registration requirements sheet and its building code amendments.

  1. Ask for the registered business name. Use it, not a sales rep's name, when you check with the city.
  2. Confirm it is current. Registration runs one year from the application date, so a company registered two years ago may have lapsed.
  3. Ask for the insurance certificate directly. The city wants proof of at least $300,000 in liability coverage; have the insurer send you a copy too.
  4. Ask whether your job needs a permit. Re-roofs are not named in the permit FAQ, but the city logs roof repair and replacement permits. Find out before work starts.
  5. Ask how the roof will meet code. Benbrook's code amendments say materials and methods for recovering or replacing a roof covering must comply with the building code's roofing chapter.

Permits and Inspections is in City Hall at 911 Winscott Road, phone 817-249-6064. Inspections are requested at 817-249-6000 a day ahead.

March 2016: a tornado on the water

In March 2016 the National Weather Service confirmed a brief EF-0 tornado near the Benbrook Lake marina, with winds estimated around 85 mph. KERA reported that it tore apart the dry dock area and shoved boats on top of one another; it was one of five tornadoes the weather service confirmed across North Texas over a single day. NBC DFW noted the damage stayed light.

An EF-0 is the weakest rating, but 85 mph is more than enough to lift shingle tabs, peel ridge caps and drop limbs onto a roof. Houses near open water or on higher ground catch gusts that sheltered streets do not, which is worth remembering when you check the roof after a spring storm.

Leave the roof to the roofer. A wet or storm-hit roof is slippery, and damaged decking can give way, so keep off it and keep the ladder put away. Stay clear of any downed power line and report it to Oncor or your local electric utility, or call 911. Inside, pull furniture and electronics away from the drip, set out a bucket or towels, and keep everyone out of a room where the ceiling is sagging. Take photos from the yard and from inside, then call your insurance company and a roofer.

No state license for roofers. Texas does not license roofing contractors. A 2025 bill that would have had the state license re-roofers (HB 3344) cleared a House committee but never got a floor vote, and it died when the session ended. That puts the checking on you: ask for a certificate of liability insurance sent to you by the roofer's insurance agent or insurer, a written contract that lists the full scope, the permit or contractor registration your city requires, addresses of nearby jobs, and proof the shingle warranty was registered. The line does none of this checking for you. How to check a roofer in Texas.

Your deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance warns that a contractor may not waive your deductible, rebate it, or pad the estimate to cover it, and that a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice that you owe the deductible. Your insurer may ask for proof you paid it. A contractor also may not act as a public adjuster on a property it works on or may work on. If a roofer offers to "take care of" the deductible, hire someone else.

What Benbrook homeowners ask about roofing

How can I tell if a roofing company in Benbrook TX is registered?

Ask the company for the name it registered under, then check with Benbrook's Permits and Inspections Department at City Hall, 911 Winscott Road, 817-249-6064. The city's registration asks for proof of at least $300,000 in liability insurance and expires a year after the application, so ask whether the registration is current. Add the usual checks from the guide to checking a Texas roofer.

Is a permit needed to reroof in Benbrook?

Benbrook's FAQ says a building permit is needed for new structures, additions and remodeling, and does not single out re-roofs. The city's permit logs do carry a roof repair and replacement category, and its code amendments set rules for recovering or replacing a roof covering. Ask Permits and Inspections about your job, and put in writing which party applies if a permit is needed.

Roofing Benbrook: what should I do right after a storm?

Keep off the roof and away from any line that is down. Inside, move what you can away from drips and put a pan under them. Photograph the damage from the ground and from inside, note the date, and call your insurer to ask about your wind and hail deductible. Then call for a roofer to inspect. The storm damage page explains what a roofer checks.
